top_stories.title: Bitcoin Rebounds to $80K After Democratic Congressional Sweep
points: Bitcoin fell to $75,600 on election night before rebounding to around $80,000-$80,530 (a 3.5% jump in 24 hours) after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in midterm elections.
The rebound was driven largely by a short squeeze, where traders who bet on price declines were forced to close positions at a loss, pushing prices higher.
Analysts noted the Democratic sweep outcome was largely priced in by markets beforehand, meaning the rebound reflected short-covering more than genuine enthusiasm for the result.
Traders assign only 57% odds of Bitcoin reaching $85,000 by November 30, 25% odds for $90,000, and just 3% probability of hitting $100,000.

unique_angles.point: Matt Corallo flagged a critical Linux kernel vulnerability directly impacting Lightning Network nodes (payment channels enabling faster Bitcoin transactions with lower fees), urging operators to take immediate action.
Ethereum and U.S. stocks rallied alongside Bitcoin, with Microsoft and Alphabet shares surging post-election while Nvidia and Tesla declined.

Crypto's legislative agenda dimmed: the Clarity Act (a bill meant to establish regulatory clarity for digital assets) stalled in the Senate in September and now faces a wary Democratic Congress, with prediction markets giving it only a 3% chance of passing this year, despite the industry spending over $300 million backing favorable candidates.

items.title: Morgan Stanley Tokenizes U.S. Stocks and Treasuries
points: Morgan Stanley began moving U.S. stocks and Treasuries onto blockchain rails, tokenizing (converting to digital form on a blockchain) traditional securities using existing Wall Street settlement systems.
The move marks a major institutional adoption milestone, bringing mainstream financial assets from one of the world's largest investment banks onto distributed ledger infrastructure.

items.title: Circle Cuts Staff Despite Profitable Quarter
points: Circle, issuer of the USDC stablecoin, quietly cut 5% of its staff despite posting profits for the quarter.
Reserve income (earnings from assets backing the stablecoin) fell 8% in the quarter, contributing to the cost-cutting move.
